# eva

A simple calculator REPL (read–eval–print loop) similar to bc(1), with syntax highlighting and persistent history.

Description

Type an expression and press Enter; the result will be printed. Repeat to continue using the REPL.

Usage

    eva [OPTIONS] [INPUT]

ARGS:
    <INPUT>    Optional expression string to run eva in command mode

OPTIONS:
    -b, --base <RADIX>    Radix of calculation output (1 - 36) [default: 10]
    -f, --fix <FIX>       Number of decimal places in output (1 - 64) [default: 10]
    -r, --radian          Use radian mode
    -h, --help            Print help information
    -V, --version         Print version information

Examples

    > 1 + sin(30)
    1.5

    > floor(sqrt(3^2 + 5^2))
    5

Operators

- Binary operators: +  -  *  /  ^  **
- Unary operators: +  -

Constants

Some mathematical constants are available (for example: pi, e).

Functions

Most common mathematical functions are available. Trigonometric functions accept input in degrees by default.

1-argument functions:

sin, cos, tan, csc, sec, cot, sinh, cosh, tanh, asin, acos, atan, acsc, asec, acot, ln, log2, log10, sqrt, ceil, floor, abs

2-argument functions:

log (base-specific), nroot

Quality of life features

- Auto insertion of implicit multiplication (e.g. 12sin(45) -> 12 * sin(45))
- Auto-balancing of parentheses
- Use previous answer with the underscore (_) symbol
- Friendly error messages for domain errors and syntax issues

```
fn read_word(s, i) -> (String, j) {
   let mut w = "";
   // leading letters
   while i < len && s[i].is_alphabetic() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
   // digits

   // then (letter digit+)*
   loop {
      if i < len && s[i].is_alphabetic() {
         // look ahead: the next char must be a digit
         if i+1 < len && s[i+1].is_digit() {
            w.push(s[i]); i += 1;
            while s[i].is_digit() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
            continue
         } else { break }
      } else { break }
   }
   (w, i)
}
```

```
fn parse_expr(&mut self) -> Result<f64, Err> {
  let mut left = self.parse_term()?;
  loop {
    match self.peek() {
      Some(Tok::Op('+')) | Some(Tok::Op('-')) => {
         let op = ...;
         self.next();
         let right = self.parse_term()?;
         left = op(left, right)?;
      }
      _ => break
    }
  }
  Ok(left)
}

fn parse_term(&mut self) -> Result<f64, Err> {
  let mut left = self.parse_factor()?;
  loop {
    match self.peek() {
      Some(Tok::Op('*')) | Some(Tok::Op('/')) | Some(Tok::Op('%')) => { ... }
      _ => break
    }
  }
  Ok(left)
}
```

```
fn read_word(s, i) -> (String, j) {
   let mut w = "";
   // leading letters
   while i < len && s[i].is_alphabetic() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }

            while s[i].is_digit() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }

         } else { break }
      } else { break }
   }
```

```
  loop {
```

```
fn read_word(s, i) -> (String, j) {
   let mut w = "";
   // leading letters
   while i < len && s[i].is_alphabetic() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
   // digits
   while i < len && s[i].is_digit() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
   // then (letter digit+)*
   loop {
      if i < len && s[i].is_alphabetic() {
         // look ahead: the next char must be a digit
         if i+1 < len && s[i+1].is_digit() {
            w.push(s[i]); i += 1;
            while s[i].is_digit() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
            continue
         } else { break }
      } else { break }
   }
   (w, i)
}
```

```
fn parse_expr(&mut self) -> Result<f64, Err> {
  let mut left = self.parse_term()?;
  loop {
    match self.peek() {
      Some(Tok::Op('+')) | Some(Tok::Op('-')) => {
         let op = ...;
         self.next();
         let right = self.parse_term()?;
         left = op(left, right)?;
      }
      _ => break
    }
  }
  Ok(left)
}

fn parse_term(&mut self) -> Result<f64, Err> {
  let mut left = self.parse_factor()?;
  loop {
    match self.peek() {
      Some(Tok::Op('*')) | Some(Tok::Op('/')) | Some(Tok::Op('%')) => { ... }
      _ => break
    }
  }
  Ok(left)
}

  ...

  if peek == Op('^') { consume; let exp = self.parse_factor()?; return pow(base, exp) }

fn parse_primary(&mut self) -> Result<f64, Err> {
  match self.next() {
    None => Err(Parse("Too many operators, too few operands")),
    Some(Tok::Num(v)) => Ok(v),
    Some(Tok::Const(c)) => Ok(c.value()),
    Some(Tok::Prev) => { if let Some(p) = self.prev { Ok(p) } else { Err(Syntax("No previous answer!")) } }

    Some(Tok::Invalid(s)) => Err(Syntax(format!("Unexpected character '{}'", s))),
    Some(Tok::DotOp) => ...
    Some(Tok::RParen) => Err(Syntax("Mismatched parentheses!")),

}
```

```
fn read_word(s, i) -> (String, j) {
   let mut w = "";
   // leading letters
   while i < len && s[i].is_alphabetic() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
   // digits
   while i < len && s[i].is_digit() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
   // then (letter digit+)*
   loop {
      if i < len && s[i].is_alphabetic() {
         // look ahead: the next char must be a digit
         if i+1 < len && s[i+1].is_digit() {
            w.push(s[i]); i += 1;
            while s[i].is_digit() { w.push(s[i]); i += 1 }
            continue
         } else { break }
      } else { break }
   }
   (w, i)
}
```

```
fn parse_expr(&mut self) -> Result<f64, Err> {
  let mut left = self.parse_term()?;
  loop {
    match self.peek() {
      Some(Tok::Op('+')) | Some(Tok::Op('-')) => {
         let op = ...;
         self.next();
         let right = self.parse_term()?;
         left = op(left, right)?;
      }
      _ => break
    }
  }
  Ok(left)
}

fn parse_term(&mut self) -> Result<f64, Err> {
  let mut left = self.parse_factor()?;
  loop {

      _ => break
    }
  }
  Ok(left)
}
```
